title: Tenant namespace shadowing caused cross-tenant KV cache contamination, eviction storm, and memory growth - follow-up
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-09 18:23 UTC a production capacity event caused a cascade of cache evictions and cross-tenant key shadowing in the KV prefix cache. Symptoms included a sharp increase in per-tenant cache misses, elevated tail latency for generation endpoints, and several customer-reported inference anomalies (incorrect prompt context observed by two tenants). The incident was rooted in a recent sharding/rehash change deployed in runtime-1.26 that changed the mix of shard keys and unintentionally allowed weak namespace separation under high churn. During autoscaling we observed concurrent reallocation of slab ownership where tombstones and transient keys were briefly visible to other tenant shards resulting in "poisoned" cache entries. The net result: eviction storms, unexpected memory growth from tombstone accumulation, and degraded SLOs for ~45 minutes before rollbacks and mitigations restored normal behavior.
timeline: 2026-02-09 18:23 UTC - First alert: cache miss rate for cluster cluster-eu-02 exceeded 12x baseline (PagerDuty).
2026-02-09 18:26 UTC - Ops runbook invoked; traffic rerouted away from affected shard set to reduce load.
2026-02-09 18:34 UTC - Temporary mitigation: disable concurrent slab rehash on autoscale (hotfix rollout rev 1.26.3).
2026-02-09 18:50 UTC - Observed memory growth plateau after tombstone sweep started; tail latency returning to normal.
2026-02-09 19:15 UTC - Full rollback of the sharding change in runtime-1.26 performed; incident declared resolved at 19:20 UTC.
2026-02-10 - Postmortem kickoff; owners assigned and initial action list created.
root_cause_analysis: Code change: rehashing logic in slab allocator (PR #8762) altered distribution of prefix keys during concurrent node joins, allowing a short window where namespace tags used for tenant isolation were not atomically set on new slab owners.

Race condition: concurrent autoscale + compaction led to stale tombstones being copied into a new shard without namespace rewrite; other tenants could resolve those tombstones as live keys (cache poisoning).
Eviction policy regression: default eviction threshold was lowered in the same release to reduce memory under normal load, which amplified eviction storms when poisoning occurred.
Observability gap: no per-tenant checksum telemetry to detect namespace crossover quickly; existing alerts were aggregate-only and delayed detection.
immediate_mitigations: Hotfix 1: Disable concurrent slab rehash during scale events (runtime-1.26.3) - rolled within 11 minutes of detection.
Hotfix 2: Increase TTL for tombstone entries in affected clusters to allow controlled sweep instead of immediate eviction.
Traffic mitigation: Diverted new session allocations from cluster-eu-02 to healthy clusters for 40 minutes to reduce churn during recovery.
Customer actions: Notified N+1 impacted customers and created scoped incident pages for 6 tenants who saw incorrect prompt context.
long_term_action_items: A1: Add atomic namespace tag assignment in rehash path to guarantee tenant isolation during slab ownership transfer - owner: Luis Ortega - estimate: 5 - due: 2026-03-10
A2: Implement per-tenant prefix checksums and an alert that triggers on any cross-tenant checksum mismatch (telemetry + alert runbook) - owner: Priya Ramesh - estimate: 8 - due: 2026-03-20
A3: Rework eviction policy to use adaptive backoff under high miss-rate surge conditions (safeguard to prevent eviction storms) - owner: Andrew Kim - estimate: 13 - due: 2026-04-05
A4: Add end-to-end chaos test for autoscale+rehash interactions in CI (including tombstone propagation scenarios) - owner: SRE Team - estimate: 8 - due: 2026-03-30
A5: Add tombstone compaction safety net that deduplicates namespace-less tombstones and logs anomalies for manual review - owner: Maya Patel - estimate: 5 - due: 2026-03-22
A6: Update runbooks: include explicit steps to disable rehashing and perform controlled tombstone sweep; add playbook for per-tenant remediation - owner: Oncall Docs - estimate: 3 - due: 2026-03-05
A7: Post-deploy canary for rehash-related changes with stricter contract tests (tenant isolation invariants) - owner: Runtime QA - estimate: 5 - due: 2026-03-18
A8: Security review: verify no sensitive cross-tenant leakage of keys or KMS material occurred; formal security audit required - owner: Security - estimate: 4 - due: 2026-03-12
accepted_risk_and_tradeoffs: Turning off concurrent slab rehash reduces autoscale ramp efficiency under extreme load but prevents transient namespace exposure; acceptable short-term tradeoff until atomic rehash is implemented.
Increasing tombstone TTL temporarily raises memory usage but allows safe, controlled sweep rather than aggressive eviction which caused customer-facing anomalies.
Adaptive eviction backoff may slightly increase latency during high-miss bursts but prioritizes correctness and avoids mass evictions and downstream SLO collapse.
validation_and_testing_plan: Unit + Integration: Add deterministic tests that simulate concurrent rehash + tenant churn with assertions on namespace invariants.
Staging Canary: Deploy rehash atomic fix to staging and run a 24h stress job with synthetic multi-tenant traffic (10k tenants) to validate no namespace leakage.
Production Canary: Phased rollout with single-cluster canary and synthetic health checks for per-tenant checksums; abort criteria defined in the canary playbook.
Observability: Deploy per-tenant checksum dashboard and alerts before any rollback removal or new release.
metrics_and_dashboards_to_add: Tombstone accumulation rate by shard and tenant
Eviction storm likelihood score (composite of miss-rate, rehash-active, and mem-pressure)
communication_and_followups: Customer Notification: Sent detailed incident summary to affected customers and offered remediation timeline - contact: solutions@redwood.ai
Internal Review: Postmortem review scheduled on 2026-03-15 15:00 UTC with Eng, SRE, Security, and PMs.
Follow-ups: Weekly check-ins for action item progress until all high-priority items are closed.
